{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-id-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"1109e794fd423d8ada07aca64343367bdf36bcd4a0f0d4ed51afbaf24bdf2672","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-id-class-d:lineage:59","source_registry_sha256":"9c432577e712960022ff656d6738a091319c6e5e4dcbdcf9429cd450e142e543","source_liveness_sha256":"eee60602368bd429216c9c2833be0be6ed9e505e5c5accebaefb9d2b9a847475"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Mountain, night and adverse-weather driving","heading":"C — Mountain, night and adverse-weather driving","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Mountain, night and adverse-weather driving

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A107
The handbook identifies Idaho's traveler service as a source for closures, roadwork, tourism, incidents, delays and weather-related road conditions. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A107
In mountains, heed speed controls and warnings about curves, steep grades and other hazards. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A107
On mountain roads, stay near the right edge to leave space from opposing traffic. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A107
Use a lower gear to control speed on a long downhill grade. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A107
Do not coast downhill in Neutral or with the clutch disengaged. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A107
Watch for a solid yellow line in the lane indicating a mountain-road no-passing area. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A107
Sound the horn before a curve on a narrow road when the view is obstructed. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A107
Do not swerve around a small animal unless certain the maneuver is safe. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A107
For a large animal on or near the road, slow and proceed cautiously because more herd animals may be nearby. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A108
If an animal enters too quickly to avoid safely, consider maintaining control through an impact as the safer alternative. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A108
Livestock being moved under control across a road have priority in Idaho. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A108
When meeting or passing a livestock herd, proceed carefully and cooperate with its handlers. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A108
The handbook describes open range as nearly all land outside city limits and herd districts where livestock customarily or by authorized grazing may roam. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A108
Fences do not establish that livestock are absent or lack priority; use extra caution in open-range areas at night. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A108
Under the handbook's stated open-range or controlled-herd collision rule, an injured or killed animal's owner is not liable for the driver's vehicle damage, and a negligent driver may be liable for the animal. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A108
At night, keep speed low enough to stop within the road distance actually visible ahead. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A109
Increase the following gap at night. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A109
Use headlights rather than parking lights between sunset and sunrise or when visibility falls below five hundred feet. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A109
At night, watch for unlit or slow vehicles, cyclists, pedestrians and animals. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A109
Allow additional time and distance when passing at night. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A109
Do not begin or continue night driving while tired, and do not wear sunglasses in low light. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A109
Keep both sides of the windshield clean and remove headlight dirt that can weaken or distort the beam. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A109
Avoid staring into approaching headlights; direct the eyes toward the lower right of the driving lane. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A109
Select low beams when approaching or following another vehicle or traveling on a lighted road. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A109
If night parking on a highway shoulder is necessary, use emergency flashers or parking lights. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A109
Keep extra caution around snow-removal equipment because thrown snow can severely restrict a close follower's visibility. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A110
The winter-driving guidance recommends staying two car lengths behind a snowplow for each ten miles an hour of speed. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A110
Pass a snowplow only when absolutely necessary and when the road ahead is clearly visible; do not pass on the snow-spraying side. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A110
Do not merge back immediately ahead of a snowplow because its blades may be hidden by snow. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A110
Avoid abrupt braking ahead of a snowplow because the heavy vehicle cannot stop as quickly as a car. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A110
Abandon a car during snow clearing only if absolutely necessary, leaving it as far off the road as possible. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A110
Low beams are best in reduced daytime visibility; check that the lights are set low when first switching them on. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A110
Avoid driving in fog, dust storms or heavy rain if possible; if driving is necessary, reduce speed. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A110
Do not use cruise control on a wet or icy road. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A110
Slow further when red taillights appear in poor visibility because the vehicle ahead may be stopped or moving very slowly. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0110]

Misconceptions: Cruise control is unsuitable for wet or icy roads, a headlight example does not guarantee visibility and ABS changes the handbook's pumping-brake instruction.
Mnemonic: Slow, see and leave space is a learning cue for the supported adverse-condition decisions.
Glossary: Hydroplaning means tires ride on water rather than road contact; open range describes qualifying livestock-grazing areas; low beams are the lower headlight setting.
Dynamic facts: current road conditions, travel-service access, seasonal adjustments and vehicle-specific equipment limits are not inferred from the frozen handbook.
